items.txt: Written in Köthen around 1720, the six suites for solo cello are dances for a single voice that still manages to sound like many. The third is the brightest: an open, ringing C major, a Sarabande of great stillness and two Bourrées that everyone hums on the way home.
Three “fantasy pieces”, written in two days in 1849. Each grows out of the one before, from the dreamy first to the fiery last, and the two players share every idea as equals.
A lament that rises to a passionate climax and falls back into silence. Fauré planned it as the slow movement of a sonata; it became one of the best-loved pieces on its own.
Brahms keeps the cello low and dark for long stretches. The sonata ends with a fugue on a theme from Bach’s Art of Fugue: a nod to the composer who opened tonight’s concert.
